newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crude prices follow WTI retreat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crude prices follow WTI retreat.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices ended lower Monday, tracking NYMEX losses that resulted from Iraq's acceptance of U.N. oil-for food deal terms.
Spot West Texas Intermediate/Cushing closed out weaker, with the January down around 25 cts at $23.50 a barrel.
Losses grew as the session progressed, but traders said the real impact of any Iraq developments would only come when the U.N. actually said oil sales had started.
The West Coast benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) was pulled lower in accordance with the WTI retreat, but business was stilted and trades were only in the talking stages.

West Coast traders said local spot markets remained exceedingly thin, with ANS discounts flat at $2.20 under January WTI. Line 63 barrels discounts were also stable in early trade at $3.15 under Jan WTI.
West Coast traders said local spot markets saw ANS valued at $2.20 under January WTI.
Buyers were firm in their position at $2.30 under the marker, but the seller was also comfortable at the $2.10 discount, traders said.
"We could do deals all day long at $2.20 (under WTI)," said one trader, but he noted 50 percent run cuts had reduced the need to make a move.
"We will not run at these levels. The flow of products supply, gasoline, cannot support the WTI to ANS numbers," said the trader.

Heavier grades were thinly discussed as well. Kern River was at flat to 5 cents above posted prices, or around $17.00/05, while Line 63 was assessed 95 cents to $1.05 above postings or $3.20 to $3.00 under Dec WTI.
